messages.subject: error in pcountOPEN: 99 sites have been discarded because of missing data.  data attached
parts:
Dear All,
I am modelling some species abundances using pcountOPEN.  I have got my models to run without covariates of detectability, but I when I add just one, I am getting the error:

1: Some observations have been discarded because corresponding covariates were missing.
2: 99 sites have been discarded because of missing data.

This is 99 of 137 sites, and I am so far at a loss to discover why it is happening... I am attaching my unmarked frame in case anyone wants to have a look, but I can also confirmed the following:

1: some of the missing sites are those at which the species definitely occurs

2: Since I have some sites visited 8 times during a primary period, and others only once or twice, padding my matrix for all possible combinations gives me I have a lot of "missing data", BUT.... there is no pattern in the number of missing survey occasions when I examine the slot "@sitesRemoved" in my problem model: some sites are missing all but one or two observations, others have about 30 observations)

3: There are no missing covariates, that is, all observations that were actually completed have the full set of obsCovs

4: There are no sites with missing sitCovs

5: I am using a data frame of MxJT rows for my obsCovs, sorted first by site then by visit.

Am I misinterpreting the way my obsCos should be ordered, or is there some other problem I am missing? Any thoughts would be much appreciated.
A

parts:
Dear Alex,

 

not sure about the missing value policy of the function, but to get a better understanding you could perhaps fill on parts of the covariate matrix to see how different patterns of missingness affect the data tossing out policy of unmarked ? Actually, I think you could probably simply fill in (e.g., using the covariate mean) all covariates and run the model, as this should not affect the parameter estimates.

 

Others : please correct if the latter suggestion is wrong.

 

Kind regards  --- Marc

Dear Marc,
Thanks for your reply.  I have tried filling in the covariate matrix, (giving the entire matrix for the test covariate a value of 1) and this model at least runs without the error, leading me to the conclusion that the problem does lie wth the way I am formatting my obsCovs, however, I know from previous model runs that there are observation-level effects which I would like to include in the model, so infilling is not a long-term solution.  Is there perhaps some problem with the way I am interpreting "site-major order" as stated in the help file? (I took this to mean ordered by site, then by observation) Best regards, and thanks for your time,
A

Dear Alex,

 

not sure about the missing value policy of the function, but to get a better understanding you could perhaps fill on parts of the covariate matrix to see how different patterns of missingness affect the data tossing out policy of unmarked ? Actually, I think you could probably simply fill in (e.g., using the covariate mean) all covariates and run the model, as this should not affect the parameter estimates.

 

Others : please correct if the latter suggestion is wrong.

 

Kind regards  --- Marc
